content.stem: A shopkeeper in Jaipur sells a printer marked at ₹3,200 to a customer in the same city, allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. GST on the printer is charged at 18%. The amount of SGST charged on the bill is:

hints: GST is charged on the price after the discount, not on the marked price.
For a sale within one state, the GST rate is split equally between CGST and SGST.

solution.modelAnswer: Selling price \(= 3200 - 15\% \text{ of } 3200 = ₹2{,}720\). The sale is intra-state, so SGST rate \(= \tfrac{18\%}{2} = 9\%\). SGST \(= 9\% \text{ of } 2720 = ₹244.80\). Option (b).

steps.title: Price after discount
steps.explanation: GST is charged on the actual selling price, which is the marked price less the discount.

steps.title: SGST rate
steps.explanation: Seller and buyer are in the same state, so the GST of 18% is shared equally as CGST 9% and SGST 9%.
steps.reason: Intra-state supply: GST = CGST + SGST, each half of the GST rate.

commonMistakes: Charging the tax on the marked price: \(9\% \text{ of } 3200 = ₹288\), option (a).
Giving the total GST \(18\% \text{ of } 2720 = ₹489.60\) instead of the SGST alone, option (c).
Halving the SGST rate again (using 4.5%), which gives ₹122.40, option (d).

questions.authorNotes: Assumes a single intra-state sale with GST split equally into CGST and SGST; all rates are stated in the stem.

content.stem:
A manufacturer M in Pune (Maharashtra) sells a consignment of water purifiers to a wholesaler W in Indore (Madhya Pradesh) for ₹20,000. W sells the consignment to a retailer R in Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) at a profit of ₹4,000. R then sells it to a consumer in Bhopal for ₹27,500.

The rate of GST is 12% at every stage. All prices are exclusive of GST, M has no input tax credit, and every dealer claims full input tax credit.

parts.prompt: State the type(s) of GST charged in sale 1 and in sale 2, and find the amount of each tax charged in these two sales.
Find the net GST payable by W to the government.
Find the CGST and SGST payable by R to the government. Hence show that the total GST received by the government from M, W and R equals the GST paid by the consumer.

hints: A sale between two different states attracts IGST; a sale within one state attracts CGST and SGST in equal halves.
A dealer pays only (tax collected on sales) − (tax paid on purchases).

solution.modelAnswer:
(a) Sale 1 is inter-state: IGST \(= 12\% \text{ of } 20000 = ₹2{,}400\). Sale 2 is intra-state at \(₹24{,}000\): CGST \(= 6\% \text{ of } 24000 = ₹1{,}440\) and SGST \(= ₹1{,}440\).

(b) W's output tax \(= 1440 + 1440 = ₹2{,}880\); input tax credit (IGST paid) \(= ₹2{,}400\). Net GST payable \(= 2880 - 2400 = ₹480\).

(c) Sale 3 is intra-state: CGST \(=\) SGST \(= 6\% \text{ of } 27500 = ₹1{,}650\). R pays CGST \(1650 - 1440 = ₹210\) and SGST \(1650 - 1440 = ₹210\). Government receives \(2400 + 480 + 420 = ₹3{,}300\), and the consumer pays GST \(= 12\% \text{ of } 27500 = ₹3{,}300\). The two are equal.
solution.finalAnswer: (a) Sale 1: IGST ₹2,400; sale 2: CGST ₹1,440 and SGST ₹1,440. (b) ₹480. (c) CGST ₹210 and SGST ₹210; total GST received by the government = ₹3,300 = GST paid by the consumer.

steps.title: Sale 1: inter-state
steps.explanation: M (Maharashtra) and W (Madhya Pradesh) are in different states, so the whole 12% is charged as IGST.
steps.rule: Inter-state supply: IGST at the full GST rate.

steps.title: Sale 2: intra-state
steps.explanation: W and R are both in Madhya Pradesh, so the 12% is split into CGST 6% and SGST 6% on W's selling price of ₹24,000.
steps.rule: Intra-state supply: CGST = SGST = half the GST rate.

steps.title: W's output and input tax
steps.explanation: W collects ₹2,880 from R and has already paid ₹2,400 IGST to M, which W can claim as input tax credit.

steps.title: Net GST payable by W
steps.explanation: W pays the government only the difference: ₹480.
steps.rule: GST payable = output tax − input tax credit

steps.title: Tax on sale 3
steps.explanation: R and the consumer are both in Madhya Pradesh, so CGST and SGST of 6% each are charged on ₹27,500.

steps.title: R's payable tax
steps.explanation: R paid CGST ₹1,440 and SGST ₹1,440 to W; these are claimed as credit against the same heads.

steps.title: Verify the total
steps.explanation: The government receives ₹2,400 from M, ₹480 from W and ₹420 from R, a total of ₹3,300. This equals the GST of 12% on the final price paid by the consumer, ₹3,300. With input tax credit, tax is collected only on the value added at each stage.

commonMistakes: Charging CGST and SGST on sale 1 even though M and W are in different states.
Charging tax on the profit only (₹4,000) instead of on W's full selling price of ₹24,000.
Forgetting input tax credit and saying W pays ₹2,880 to the government.

alternativeMethods.title: Tax on value added
alternativeMethods.description: With full input tax credit, each dealer's GST payable is 12% of the value it adds: W adds \(₹4{,}000\), so it pays \(12\% \text{ of } 4000 = ₹480\); R adds \(27500 - 24000 = ₹3{,}500\), so it pays \(12\% \text{ of } 3500 = ₹420\), split equally as CGST ₹210 and SGST ₹210.

rubric.notes: Allow follow-through in (b) and (c) from an incorrect value in (a), provided the method is correct.

criteria.description: Identifies sale 1 as inter-state and finds IGST
Identifies sale 2 as intra-state and finds CGST and SGST on ₹24,000
Uses output tax − input tax credit for W
Correct net GST payable by W
Finds CGST and SGST on sale 3
Finds R's CGST and SGST payable
Shows total GST received by the government equals GST paid by the consumer
commonErrors: Adds the tax charged at every stage (2400 + 2880 + 3300) instead of the tax paid

questions.authorNotes: Follows the usual textbook treatment: IGST on an inter-state sale, equal CGST/SGST on an intra-state sale, and full input tax credit. Part (b) asks only for W's total net GST because splitting an IGST credit between CGST and SGST depends on credit-utilisation rules that are outside the scope of the question; a reviewer may wish to keep it that way. Place names are used only to show which sales are inter-state.
